mainTopic: Counting ages and time periods: end-points of a range, רבי אליעזר's extra month and day, and periods counted מעת לעת
overview: This amud deals with how to count ages and time periods. First, a ברייתא about חמץ asks whether a range like 'from the first day to the seventh' includes its end-points, the way 'from his head to his feet' leaves out the head and feet of a מצורע. רבי says end-points are obviously included. The גמרא then asks why רבי needs a גזירה שוה for the border years in ערכין, and answers that the ערכין פסוקים cancel each other out. Next the גמרא gives two sources for leaving out the head and feet in צרעת. It then brings רבי אליעזר's view that a person changes ערכין age group only a month and a day past the birthday, learned from the census of the לויים. A new ברייתא lists Torah time periods counted from the exact start date and not by the calendar, and the גמרא finds a פסוק for each one. Finally, רב and רב יוסף explain the 'son and daughter' item differently, ערכין or the פרק יוצא דופן, and the גמרא shows they do not really disagree. רב יוסף's answer to רב's reasoning continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the end-points are left out, as with the head and feet of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that the first and seventh days of the חמץ ban might be left out, just like the head and feet in the case of צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is like what is said about a מצורע: 'from his head to his feet.' That means up to the head, but not the head itself, and up to the feet, but not the feet themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe a range like 'from the first day to the seventh day' leaves out both ends. It is setting up the next move, where a פסוק will answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With צרעת, the words 'from his head to his feet' mean that the head and feet themselves are not counted. The ברייתא worries that the days of פסח might work the same way, so the first and seventh days would not be part of the חמץ ban.

keyTerms.meaning: included (inside the range)
like the matter that is stated (a comparison to another פסוק)
the skin disease of the Torah (a 'מצורע' is the person who has it)

steps.confusionAlert: This piece is the middle of a ברייתא about חמץ on פסח. The 'head and feet' line is only brought as a comparison. The real topic behind all of this is whether the 20th year belongs to the earlier age group in ערכין.

phrases.english: Like the matter that is stated: "from his head to his feet"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:12. This is about צרעת covering a person's whole body. It is being compared to the days of פסח.

phrases.english: his head, but his head is not included;
his feet, but his feet are not included?

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּעִנְיָן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the first and seventh days included in the חמץ ban, or are they left out like the head and feet of a מצורע?

steps.title: A פסוק shows the seventh day is included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with a פסוק: 'until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.' This shows the last day is included.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says: 'until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק that shows the ban goes all the way to the end of the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'until the evening of the 21st' makes it clear that the whole 21st day, the seventh day of פסח, is inside the ban. So the end-point here is included, unlike the head and feet of a מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse teaches (introduces a פסוק that answers the question)
in the evening

phrases.english: The verse states:
"until the twenty-first day of the month in the evening."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:18

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the possibility raised in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'until the 21st in the evening' shows that the seventh day is included.

steps.title: רבי holds that end-points are included without any פסוק, so why does he need a גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי says no פסוק is needed, because the first and seventh days are obviously included. The גמרא uses this against רבי's need for a גזירה שוה about the 20th year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: That פסוק is not needed. 'First' means the first day is included, and 'seventh' means the seventh day is included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי's opinion from the ברייתא to challenge him. If he thinks end-points are included on their own, why does he need a גזירה שוה to include the 20th year in ערכין?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, a range naturally includes both of its ends. If so, the phrase 'until twenty years' in ערכין should already put year 20 in the earlier group. That makes the גזירה שוה he uses look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not needed
a teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not arguing about the הלכה of פסח. Everyone agrees the seventh day is included. The disagreement is only about whether a פסוק is needed to teach it.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: It is not necessary;
"first" — and the first day is included;
"seventh" — and the seventh day is included!
phrases.notes: This is a challenge: if the last day counts, רבי shouldn't need a גזירה שוה to include year 20 in ערכין.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the end of the ברייתא as a challenge to רבי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's use of a גזירה שוה to include the 20th year in the earlier age group in ערכין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי holds that the ends of a range are included anyway, the גזירה שוה is unnecessary.

steps.title: The ערכין פסוקים cancel each other out
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי needs the גזירה שוה, because in ערכין the פסוקים pull in opposite directions about the border years.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say this follows רבי, because the פסוקים balance each other out. It is written 'from one month old until five years old.' Why also write 'from five years old until twenty'? So the two cancel each other out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In ערכין, the same border age appears in two groups, so we cannot tell where it belongs without the גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Year five ends one age group and starts the next one. So רבי's rule that 'the end is included' gives two opposite answers, and the two פסוקים cancel each other out. Since the פסוקים alone settle nothing, רבי still needs the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say (that it fits this opinion too)
the פסוקים balance each other out
since (now look at this)
therefore

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי, who holds that the ends of a range are included, needs the גזירה שוה in ערכין, because there the פסוקים cancel each other out.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi,
because the verses balance each other out.
Since it is written:
"from one month old until five years old"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:6

phrases.aramaic: תּוּ ״מִבֶּן חָמֵשׁ וְעַד בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים״ לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: why do I also need "from five years old until twenty years old"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:5. Year five shows up in both groups.

phrases.english: Therefore they cancel each other out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the general rule cannot be applied here because the פסוקים conflict.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's rule that end-points are included should already decide the border year in ערכין.
steps.terutzMaskana: In ערכין the border year appears in two groups, so the פסוקים cancel out and the גזירה שוה is needed even for רבי.

steps.title: How do we know the head and feet of a מצורע are not included?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's line about the head and feet of a מצורע and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'His head, but not his head itself; his feet, but not his feet themselves.' How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a side detail from the ברייתא and asks where that rule about צרעת comes from. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a range might include its ends, as רבי held about פסח. So the גמרא wants to know why, with צרעת, the head and feet are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?

phrases.english: The Master said:
"his head" — but his head is not included;
"his feet" — but his feet are not included.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the comparison in step 1 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for leaving out the head and feet in the case of צרעת.

steps.title: First answer: the signs on the head differ from the signs on the body
steps.stepSummary: The head has different signs of צרעת than the body, so it cannot be counted together with the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: the signs of צרעת on the body are different from the signs on the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer based on reasoning: the head follows different rules of צרעת, so it is not part of the 'whole body' range.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the head has its own signs of צרעת, a rule about the body cannot simply include the head. So 'from his head' means starting below the head.

keyTerms.meaning: if you want, say (introduces one possible answer)
is different
signs (that show whether it is צרעת)

phrases.english: If you want, say:
the signs of his body are different
from the signs of his head.
phrases.notes: He means the hair signs: the head has its own rules for which hair color shows צרעת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: שָׁאנֵי סִימָנִים דְּגוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Logic: the head has separate signs of צרעת, so it is not included with the body.

steps.title: Second answer: 'wherever the כהן can see'
steps.stepSummary: Another source: the פסוק says 'wherever the כהן can see', which leaves out places that are hard to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: it comes from the words 'wherever the כהן can see.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer, this time from words in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only counts areas that the כהן can see. The head, which is covered by hair, and the feet, between the toes, are not easy to see, so they are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: wherever the כהן can see

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons the head and feet are not included with צרעת: the head has different signs, or the פסוק only counts what the כהן can see.

phrases.english: Or, if you want, say:
"wherever the priest can see."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:12, the same פסוק as "from his head to his feet."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְכׇל מַרְאֵה עֵינֵי הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק: 'wherever the כהן can see' leaves out areas that are hard to see.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר adds a month and a day to each age
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה where רבי אליעזר says the person stays in the earlier age group until a month and a day past the birthday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: the person stays in the earlier group until they are a month and one day past those years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to רבי אליעזר's opinion in the משנה, so it can look for his source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא of the משנה moves a person into the new age group right after the birthday. רבי אליעזר disagrees: you only switch groups after one extra month and one extra day.

keyTerms.meaning: more than, beyond
a month and one day
pledges of a person's fixed 'value' to the Temple, set by age and gender

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
until they are beyond the years
phrases.notes: "The years" means the border ages in ערכין: five, twenty and sixty.

phrases.english: by a month and one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ יְתֵירוֹת עַל הַשָּׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the head and feet of a מצורע and back to the משנה's dispute about the border years.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a person enters the next ערכין age group only after a month and one day past the birthday.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: a word link to the census of the Levites
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר learns his view from a גזירה שוה between 'upward' in ערכין and 'a month and upward' in the Levite census.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, here it says 'upward', and there it says 'a month and upward'. Just as there it means from a month and one day old, so too here it means from a month and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for רבי אליעזר's extra month and day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'upward' (מעלה) shows up both in ערכין and in the counting of the לויים. There, 'a month and upward' means a baby who is a month and one day old. So in ערכין too, 'upward' means a month and one day past the stated age.

keyTerms.meaning: here, meaning in the פסוק we are learning (ערכין)
there, meaning in the other פסוק being compared
upward, the shared word that links the two פסוקים

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
It says here "upward,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:7, about ערכין.

phrases.english: and it says there "a month and upward,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 3:15, the counting of the לויים.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: just as there it means from a month and one day old,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן מִבֶּן חוֹדֶשׁ וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too here it means from a month and one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for the view quoted in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that each age group starts a month and one day after the birthday.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word 'upward' between ויקרא 27:7 and במדבר 3:15.

steps.title: Why not compare only the one extra day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the comparison should copy just the one extra day from the census, not a whole month and a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is like there: just as there it is one day more, so too here it should be one day more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges how רבי אליעזר uses the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the census, the one month is the age itself, and only the one day is 'extra'. So if ערכין copies the census, maybe it should copy only the extra day, so the new group starts one day after the fifth, twentieth or sixtieth birthday. Why add a whole month?

keyTerms.meaning: but let us say, an opening for a different possible reading
like there
one day

phrases.english: But say it is like there:
just as there it is one day more,
phrases.notes: In the census, the age is one month, and only one day is added on top.

phrases.english: so too here it should be one day more?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא כִּי הָתָם, מָה הָתָם חַד יוֹמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way step 9 applies the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's claim that the גזירה שוה adds a month and a day in ערכין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the census only one day is added past the stated age, so the comparison should add only one day.

steps.title: Adding one day would make the word link pointless
steps.stepSummary: If only one day were added, we would not need the גזירה שוה at all, so it must be teaching a month and a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what did the גזירה שוה accomplish?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by asking what the גזירה שוה would be for if it only added one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without any comparison, we would know that a new group starts the day after the year ends. A גזירה שוה has to teach something new, so it must be teaching the extra month and day.

keyTerms.meaning: if so
what did it accomplish? (what is it for?)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר learns a month and a day, not just one day, because a גזירה שוה must teach something we could not know by ourselves.

phrases.english: If so,
what did the word comparison accomplish!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מַאי אַהֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the other reading would leave the גזירה שוה with nothing to teach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison adds only one day, like the census.
steps.terutzMaskana: One extra day is obvious anyway, so the גזירה שוה must be adding a month and a day.

steps.title: A list of Torah time periods counted from the actual start date
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists several Torah time periods (קדשים, houses in walled cities, an inherited field, an עבד עברי, son and daughter) that are all counted from the exact starting day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: the year stated about sacrifices, the year stated about houses in walled cities, the two years of an inherited field, the six years of a Hebrew slave, and likewise those of a son and a daughter, are all counted from the exact time to the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how to count years in different areas of the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these periods is counted as full years from the day it began, not by the calendar year (for example, ending at ראש השנה). The גמרא will now look for a source for each item in the list.

keyTerms.meaning: from time to time, a full period from the exact start date
sacrifices
houses in walled cities, which can be bought back within one year
an inherited family field
a Jewish servant who works for six years

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
the year stated regarding sacrifices,
the year stated regarding houses in walled cities,
the two years of an inherited field,
and the six years of a Hebrew slave,
and likewise those of a son and a daughter
all of them are counted from the exact time to the same time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּקָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected because it is also about counting years and ages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All these Torah periods are counted as full years from the actual start date, not by the calendar year.
steps.confusionAlert: מעת לעת here does not mean counting hours. It means the year runs from the starting date to the same date the next year, not until the next ראש השנה.

steps.title: Where do we learn the year of sacrifices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the year of קדשים is counted from the animal's own birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The year stated about sacrifices, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא's list, asking for the source of the first item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the rule but no source. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that an animal's 'year' runs from its own birth.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?

phrases.english: The year stated regarding sacrifices, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּקָדָשִׁים, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first item in the ברייתא of step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that the year of קדשים is counted from the animal's own birth date.

steps.title: 'Its year' means the animal's own year
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns from the words 'a sheep in its year' that the year is counted from the animal's birth, not by the calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: the פסוק says 'a sheep in its year', meaning its own year, and not the year of the world's count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a precise reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says 'its year' (שנתו), not 'the year'. That word shows the year belongs to the animal, so it starts from the animal's birth. It is not the calendar year everyone counts together.

keyTerms.meaning: a sheep in its (first) year
the world's count, the calendar year

steps.whatToRemember: For קדשים, an animal's year starts from its own birth, learned from the word 'שנתו', its year.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
the verse says: "a sheep in its year,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:6

phrases.english: its year means its own year,
and not the year of the world's count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, אָמַר קְרָא: ״כֶּבֶשׂ בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'שנתו' (its year) shows the year is counted from the animal's own birth, not by the calendar.

steps.title: Houses in walled cities: the year counts from the sale
steps.stepSummary: The year for redeeming a house in a walled city is counted from the day of its own sale, not by the calendar year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The year mentioned for houses in walled cities: as it is written, 'until the end of the year of its sale.' That means its own sale, and not the regular calendar year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the ברייתא and gives the פסוק that shows the house's year starts on the day it was sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מִמְכָּרוֹ, 'its sale', ties the year to this particular sale. So the year is a full twelve months from that day. It does not end when the calendar year ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Its sale

phrases.english: The year stated regarding houses of walled cities —
as it is written: 'Until the end of the year of its sale,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:29

phrases.english: its own sale,
and not the year of the world's counting.
phrases.notes: He means it is not the calendar year that everyone counts by.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁנָה הָאֲמוּרָה בְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the pattern from step 14 by giving the source for the next item in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The walled-city house year runs from the day of sale, not by the calendar.

steps.title: Inherited field: three crops in two years
steps.stepSummary: The two years for an inherited field are counted from the sale, so a buyer can sometimes harvest three crops in two years.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two years mentioned for an inherited field: as it is written, 'according to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.' Sometimes a person eats three crops in two years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source showing that the two years of an inherited field are counted from the day it was bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'years of crops,' and the גמרא points out that the number of crops can be more than the number of years. That can only happen if the count runs from the sale. If the count followed the calendar, a new year would begin soon after the purchase.

keyTerms.meaning: Crops or harvests
Sometimes

phrases.english: The two years of an inherited field,
as it is written: 'According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:15

phrases.english: there are times that a person eats
three crops in two years.
phrases.notes: Picture buying the field right before a harvest: he eats that crop and two more, all before two full years are up.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים שֶׁבִּשְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list, with its own פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two years of a שדה אחוזה are counted from the sale, so they can include three harvests.

steps.title: Hebrew slave: sometimes he works into the seventh year
steps.stepSummary: The six years of an עבד עברי are full years from his sale, so he may sometimes keep working into the seventh calendar year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The six years of a Hebrew slave: as it is written, 'six years he shall work, and in the seventh...' Sometimes he works in the seventh year too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows from the פסוק that the עבד עברי's six years are counted from the day he was sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'and' in 'and in the seventh' hints that part of the seventh calendar year can still be work time. This happens when six full years have not yet passed since his sale. So he goes free on the anniversary of his sale, not at the start of a calendar year.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year
Sometimes

phrases.english: The six years of a Hebrew slave —
as it is written: 'Six years he shall work, and in the seventh,'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:2

phrases.english: sometimes he will work in the seventh as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֵׁשׁ שֶׁבְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list, with its own פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד עברי serves six full years from his sale, which can stretch into the seventh calendar year.

steps.title: Son and daughter: which law is this about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last item, son and daughter, also counted from the exact day. Then it asks which law this refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: And those of the son and of the daughter: all of these are counted from the exact time. For which law is this said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the last item in the ברייתא and asks what practical law it is about. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other items each had a clear topic and a פסוק. 'Son and daughter' does not say which law depends on their age. So the גמרא asks what that law is.

keyTerms.meaning: For which law? Asking what practical rule a statement refers to

phrases.english: And those of the son and of the daughter
all of them are from time to time.
phrases.notes: This closes the whole list from step 12: every item is counted from its exact starting day.

phrases.english: For which law?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי הִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding sources for the other items, the גמרא asks about the last one, which has no clear topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law depends on the age of a son or daughter counted in full years.

steps.title: רב: it refers to ערכין
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב גידל, says the son and daughter item is about ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גידל said in the name of רב: it is for ערכין (valuations).
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: the rule about son and daughter is about ערכין, the subject of our מסכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of a person's ערך depends on age. רב teaches that the age is counted in full years from the day of birth, not by calendar years.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuations: set amounts pledged to the בית המקדש, based on a person's age and gender

phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav said:
For valuations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב לַעֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son and daughter rule is about ערכין: their age is counted from birth in full years.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it refers to the פרק of יוצא דופן
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the son and daughter item is about the ages discussed in the פרק called יוצא דופן in מסכת נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: it is for the פרק of 'יוצא דופן'.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer: the rule refers to the ages of boys and girls taught in the פרק יוצא דופן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That פרק discusses laws that depend on a child's age. רב יוסף says those ages are also counted in full years from birth. The difference between the two answers is which set of laws the ברייתא is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born through the side (by caesarean); also the name of the fifth פרק of מסכת נדה
Our פרק; a chapter of משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Every period in the ברייתא is counted מֵעֵת לְעֵת, from the exact starting day. For son and daughter, רב says this is about ערכין and רב יוסף says it is about the פרק of יוצא דופן.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
For the chapter of 'Yotze Dofen.'
phrases.notes: A פרק in מסכת נדה, named after its first words, about laws that depend on a child's age.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר לְפִרְקִין דְּיוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 18. Steps 21–23 show it does not actually disagree with step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The son and daughter rule is about the age-based laws in the פרק יוצא דופן of נדה.

steps.title: אביי asks if רב יוסף and רב really disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether he and רב are arguing about what the 'son and daughter' item refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Do you and רב disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי hears two different explanations, one from רב and one from רב יוסף, and asks whether this is a true argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said ערכין and רב יוסף said יוצא דופן. אביי wants to know whether each one rejects the other's case, or whether both cases could be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: You (plural) disagree

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Do you disagree?
phrases.notes: 'You' is plural here: רב יוסף and רב, whose view was quoted by רב גידל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף: מִי פְּלִיגִיתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the relationship between the two answers given in steps 19 and 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב and רב יוסף hold opposite views or are giving two cases that can both be true.

steps.title: רב יוסף says there is no argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that there is no disagreement. Each of them mentioned a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. I said one thing and he said another thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that he and רב are not arguing. Each one simply named a different example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'from the exact day' rule for a son and daughter can apply to both ערכין and יוצא דופן. רב mentioned one application and רב יוסף mentioned another, and neither one rules out the other.

keyTerms.meaning: One (thing or matter)

steps.confusionAlert: Two different answers in the גמרא are not always an argument. Here both answers are correct together.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא אֲמַרִי חֲדָא, וְהוּא אֲמַר חֲדָא.
phrases.english: I said one thing, and he said one thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, אֲנָא אֲמַרִי חֲדָא, וְהוּא אֲמַר חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no argument. Both cases follow the same rule, and each sage simply mentioned a different one.

steps.title: Proof that רב also applies the rule to יוצא דופן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב יוסף's answer: רב himself rules that the whole פרק יוצא דופן is counted from the exact day.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you thought they disagree, would the one who says ערכין not also say יוצא דופן? But רב himself said: the הלכה in that whole פרק is from the exact moment to the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that there is no argument. רב, who said ערכין, also holds the full-year rule for יוצא דופן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב disagreed with רב יוסף, he would hold that יוצא דופן is not counted from the exact day. But רב rules that the whole פרק works מעת לעת. So רב agrees with רב יוסף's case, and the two views fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
It enters your mind, you might think
The practical הלכה
Chapter (here, the פרק יוצא דופן in נדה)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב rules practically that the ages in יוצא דופן are counted in full years from birth, not by calendar years.

phrases.english: So too it stands to reason,
for if it enters your mind that they disagree,
the one who says it is about ערכין,
does he not say it about יוצא דופן?
But didn't רב say:
The הלכה in that whole perek is from the exact moment to the same moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's claim that there is no argument.
steps.raayaObject: That רב and רב יוסף do not disagree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's own ruling that the whole פרק יוצא דופן is counted מעת לעת.

steps.title: Why did רב choose ערכין and not יוצא דופן?
steps.stepSummary: If רב agrees about יוצא דופן, the גמרא asks why he explained the item as ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, according to the one who says ערכין, why did he not say יוצא דופן?
steps.whatsHappening: Since both cases are correct, the גמרא asks why רב picked ערכין as his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know רב agrees with the יוצא דופן rule, his choice of ערכין needs a reason. The גמרא is looking for what made ערכין the better fit for this list.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: But then, according to the one who says it is about ערכין,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר לְ״יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן״?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say it is about יוצא דופן?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לַעֲרָכִין, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר לְ״יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the proof that רב also holds the יוצא דופן rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב read the 'son and daughter' item as ערכין and not יוצא דופן.

steps.title: The list only includes ages written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב matched the item to the rest of the list, whose numbers are written in the Torah, like the ages of ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should be like the others. Just as those are written in the Torah, so too these are written in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב chose ערכין because every other item in the list has numbers written in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other items, like the years of an inherited field and of an עבד עברי, are written in the Torah. The ages of ערכין are also written in the Torah, but the ages in יוצא דופן are not. So the 'son and daughter' item fits the list best as ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to, like
That are written (in the Torah)
Just as ... so too (a comparison)

phrases.english: It is similar to those,
phrases.notes: 'Those' means the other items in the list, like the field and the עבד עברי.

phrases.english: just as those are written,
so too these are written.
phrases.notes: He means written in the Torah. The ages of ערכין appear in ויקרא 27.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּהָנָךְ, מָה הָנָךְ דִּכְתִיבָא, אַף הָנָךְ דִּכְתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why רב chose ערכין.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The item should match the rest of the list, which only contains numbers written in the Torah, and ערכין fits that pattern.

steps.title: רב יוסף's view begins: the wording does not fit ערכין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב יוסף would respond, and he begins to argue that the wording 'of a son and of a daughter' does not fit ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רב יוסף? If you think the item is about ages written in the Torah, then this wording, 'of a son and of a daughter'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רב יוסף does not accept רב's reasoning. His argument begins here and continues in the next lines of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף points to the exact wording of the ברייתא, 'of a son and of a daughter'. He is starting to show that if the item were about ערכין, this phrase would not be the right way to say it. The rest of his point comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, רב יוסף)
Of a son and of a daughter (the wording in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רב יוסף. How would he answer the reasoning just given for רב?

phrases.english: If it enters your mind that it is about things written in the Torah,
this phrase 'of a son and of a daughter'...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, אִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דִּכְתִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב יוסף's response to the reasoning offered for רב in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the item as ערכין based on the 'written in the Torah' pattern.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא's wording 'of a son and of a daughter' does not fit ערכין. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
